summary: Dedicated pool throughput dip coincident with repeated GPU evictions and aggressive autoscale churn
description: Issue summary: BeaconAI reports recurring throughput degradation in their Dedicated pool that began 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC. Impact: sustained token throughput drop (~40%) for production inference routes, increased tail latency and client-side stream disconnects. Customer impact: some user-facing features timed out; they flagged as critical. Observed at: spike of pod evictions, ephemeral GPU reallocations, and autoscaler rapidly scaling up/down over ~45 minutes. Initial hypothesis: host-level GPU evictions (kernel OOM or maintenance) causing scheduler to reassign workloads while autoscaler reacts aggressively, producing queueing and cold-start latency. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, and follow-up changes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route steady production traffic through BeaconAI dedicated pool (~120 qps total)
2) Observe autoscaler policy set with min_replicas=2, target_utilization=0.7, burst_enabled=true
3) Simulate a host-level GPU eviction (e.g., node drain or inducing OOM) on one node with A100 GPUs
4) Watch scheduler reschedule pods and autoscaler scale up to replace perceived capacity loss
5) Note transient queueing at API gateway and increased tail latency during the churn

investigation_notes: Initial metrics: GPU util per-node dropped from 65% -> 5% on evicted node; remaining nodes saw a temporary util bump to 95% leading to throttling of inference threads
Grafana dashboards: logs and metrics at dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/pool-beacon (customer link shared privately)
Kernel/OOM evidence present on host01 and host03 in the same rack; dmesg shows repeated memory reclaim and 'oom_reaper' activity
Scheduler behavior: pods were rescheduled to nodes that already had high GPU allocation causing contention (noisy-neighbor), observed via 'nvidia-smi topo -m' and pod GPU allocation tags
Autoscaler configuration: aggressive ramp (scale delta up to +4) with no stabilization window, causing rapid churn and cold-cache instances being created
Serving runtime impact: KV/prefix cache misses and model weights reloading incurred warmup overhead (~6s per pod) leading to increased per-request latency
No evidence customer-side request pattern changed; traffic steady. No recent model config changes in BeaconAI account.
comments: 2026-03-10 00:12 - Maya Patel (support): Acknowledged customer report, opened incident, requested SRE to confirm host-level events. Shared initial graphs and asked for prioritized investigation.

2026-03-10 01:05 - Arjun Singh (SRE): Confirmed OOM records on host01 and host03. Node-level memory pressure looks correlated with a noisy system job on host03 (backup job). Tentative hypothesis: system job consumed RAM leading to GPU eviction cascade.
2026-03-10 02:40 - Eng (serving-runtime): Observed cold-cache penalty on new replicas; suggested lowering autoscale aggressiveness and enabling warm-pool for BeaconAI as a short-term mitigation.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Maya Patel (support): Customer accepted temporary mitigation (increase min_replicas to 4 and disable burst scaling). They're monitoring for client errors.
resolution: Short-term mitigations applied: increased min_replicas for beacon-dedicated-1 from 2 -> 4 to maintain warm capacity; disabled burst scaling for the pool; scheduled drain of host03 to investigate system backup job.
Workaround outcome: token throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline within 12 minutes after changes; client-side stream disconnects reduced significantly.

Planned long-term fixes: (1) add autoscaler stabilization window and max-scale-step to prevent overshoot, (2) add host-level QoS constraints to prevent system backups from causing OOM on GPU hosts, (3) implement warm-pool feature for Dedicated pools to maintain warm replicas during noisy scenarios, (4) add eviction-tolerance flag on pool configs.
Follow-ups: schedule change request with infra to prevent noisy system jobs on GPU nodes; create automation to detect repeated evictions and pause autoscale actions until stabilization.
next_steps: 1) SRE to complete host postmortem and remediate noisy backup job (assigned infra tickets)
2) Product to approve autoscaler policy change and add max-scale-step and stabilization windows (tracked in GH issue)
3) Engineering to prototype warm-pool and eviction-tolerance features with BeaconAI as early adopter
4) Support to coordinate customer communication and confirm SLA impact and credits if applicable
